When you you know, analyze defensive linemen, how much does that kind of play a role into things? And is there, you know, certain circumstances where a player's tape could, you know, overmatch any, you know, quote unquote sure arms? >> Yeah, I I think I think what, you know, how the guy plays always overrides everything. So, let's let's, you know, start with that. Um, but I do think this, we've got a lot of data um that tells us what plays in the NFL, and this isn't exclusive to um the defensive line. It's all the positions. We know what plays in the NFL and we have some some measurements that that that we can look at and say, "Man, that's an outlier." We're not looking for outliers. You know, I I say this to our guys, I've said this over the years, if we are looking for exceptions, then we're not going to be here very long because exceptions are exceptions. So, we're not looking for exceptions. But we recognize that there are exceptions. And so if someone has uh some traits that don't match what plays in the NFL, then we better have some other things that tell us that he can overcome that. And so um yeah, that's my answer to that. >> You staying at number eight in this year's drafts. How much do you like his position in the draft? How is it for this particular class? Well, I don't like it because it mean it means that last year didn't go very well. So, um you don't want to be picking in the top 10, but once you know, you get to the draft and you look at the quality of the players that exist. Um yeah, you get excited about I know we're going to get a really good player at at pick eight. Um so, you get excited about that. A guy that can have an impact on your team. >> Yeah. How do you guys like define the unknowns that you can't maybe see on film? like a guy that you think might be able to rush a passer but he's only maybe has like 20 snaps of it or someone you think might be able to drop back but hasn't done a whole lot of it. >> Um well I think that gets back to traits versus you know what you've actually seen and and look this is where sometimes the off season comes into play in terms of the workouts the the the measurables you know the things that tell you yeah a guy can do something that maybe he hasn't been asked to do yet. Um, and there's it's a balance, right? It's a balance. >> Where uh, do you look at I guess your thought process is you talked about the exceptions. Picking in the top 10, you don't do that that often. Are you more prone to be we follow certain guidelines in the top 10, maybe we could be a little bit more exceptions at 28 than we could at 8? >> Yeah, I think you're I think for us, we're probably a little more risk averse. Um, you know, when we when we make a pick there, we want to have a lot of the questions answered uh about a player. You don't want to pick a player that you have a ton of questions about and you're just, you know, banking on on uh, you know, the unknown. Um, so I I think as you go farther back in the draft, you're a little more willing to take a chance on someone. Um, but I think in, you know, when you're in the top 10 or top 12, whatever the number is, you want to, uh, pick players that you have, um, as little doubt as possible that they're going to be successful. >> Does the timer going from 10 minutes to 8 minutes in the first round change like the leg work you have to do on trades and stuff ahead of the draft? >> No, I I don't really I mean, I don't know yet. I mean, we went from 15 to 10 at one point, and I didn't feel like that had a big impact. Um, I I don't think it will, but we'll see. Um, >> yeah, we'll see what happens. >> A couple positions >> that make this trap a little deeper. Um, you know, I I don't know that I can say that because deeper than what I meant, you know, last year or the year before or, you know, obviously there's fewer quarterbacks being talked about in the first round, so that changes the dynamic a little bit, but you know, and and I I hear sometimes, you know, ah, this isn't a very deep draft. I seem like I hear that every year from different people and I kind of feel like that's a little bit of an excuse that if the draft doesn't go well. Um I think there's good players in every draft. I think there's guys that are going to be Pro Bowl type players and it's our job to identify them and then hopefully we have an opportunity to take them. >> Hey Mickey, you had uh your staff a lot of your staff senior bowl time as coach. >> Yeah. >> Um did you feel like you had a head start on everybody else? Do you try to have a beat on that when you're value? >> No, I think it just changes and stuff like that. >> Um, not really. Uh, I mean, I'll ask that question now and then of Jeff and say, "Hey, what does next year look like in terms of a position or or overall, but I don't know that it's a it's a u it's not that prominent in terms of when we're we're making those discussions just because things change so much over the course of uh uh the college season." on the opposite side of that. How does that alter and make you want to have a proper class to follow them up this year? >> Yeah, I mean I I don't think it changes anything. We always want to have a great draft class. Um, you know, I thought it was great for our scouts and and Jeff and and his uh people to get recognized for for last year's success. Um, but it doesn't have any impact on what we're doing this year. >> Yesterday, um, Tyler Shuck talked about like how he's been evaluating receivers like how much input do you all let him have like how involved his head? You know, so we asked questions of all our guys. It wasn't just Tyler. Um, >> you know, it's everybody on our team that has a crossover with a player that's in this draft that we may have um an interest in in. How many scenarios do you guys prepare for? Like what's your like you know >> how many mock drafts do we do >> like a hundred >> when there when there's new like trade rumors? We can just push a button and do mock drafts. We don't have to, you know, bring all of our scouts in a room and assign them teams and then they make the pick. you know, we have this technology that allows us to uh to do these mock drafts and and we do a lot of them. We do um and so there's a lot of different scenarios, particularly in the uh the mid to later rounds, you know, because that's that's where it gets a little I don't want to say dicey, but that's probably the only word I can think of um as to what may happen. uh Sean Peyton's involvement in the draft was pretty obvious and then and then it seemed like Dennis Allen as well and he had been here for so long and the collaborative what what was your philosophy and what is your philosophy when you bring in Kell Moore is new to the organization never been a head coach are you right away like you know I want you to have as strong a voice in this as anyone is it more this year than last year like how how >> it was no different than when Sean first got us got with us right he was a new coach and I want the coaches involved I want them. You know, our goal is to all be on the same page in terms of the players that we bring in here because that gives them and us the best chance for them to be successful in my opinion. when it comes to weighing things with what you all were able to accomplish in in free agency. Is that has that shifted anything with just like your like how you're evaluating some prospects? What what maybe you be or more out of that especially with the right pick? I assume you wanted to be a starter on the team. >> Yeah, I I think it it look it certainly affects us in terms of as we get later in the draft, you know, you're trying to, you know, fill slots on your roster. I don't think it impacts us so much at the top of the draft because, you know, we're looking to take the best player that's available to us when we pick.
